title: Universal specialization lifting characterizes universal closedness
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Then $f$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism] if and only if it is quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and satisfies the following condition: for every morphism $S\prime\to S$, write $f\prime:X\times_SS\prime\to S\prime$ for the base change [def-pc-fibre-product]; for every $x\in X\times_SS\prime$ and every specialization $f\prime(x)\rightsquigarrow s$ in $S\prime$, there is a specialization $x\rightsquigarrow x\prime$ with $f\prime(x\prime)=s$. Here $a\rightsquigarrow b$ means that $b$ belongs to the closure of $\{a\}$.
